measurements.interpretation: No materialization advantage when every capability body is relevant; timing difference is not treated as meaningful from one run.

failedRun.cause: benchmark reporter referenced a wrong variable name after all 13 workload/unit tests had already passed
failedRun.repair: corrected saved-byte field and added a CLI regression test covering both a savings case and the report no-savings case

strongestSupportedClaim: For this deterministic parsed/indexed workspace harness, on-demand materialization preserved exact results and substantially reduced derived runtime allocation and materialization time when requests used only a subset of capability bodies. When all seven bodies were relevant, the materialization saving was exactly zero.
boundaries: This is one deterministic synthetic software workspace, not a production repository corpus.
One GitHub Actions measurement per scenario is not a statistical performance benchmark.
The benchmark does not yet measure warm-cache reuse across repeated requests.
The benchmark does not prove lower CPU cost for all workloads or all request breadths.
The benchmark does not prove created RAM, free compute, or free energy.
The broad report is a demonstrated no-savings case for materialized bytes.
nextGate: Add repeated-run/warm-cache modes plus a direct non-Ignition baseline to measure allocation churn, reuse, and the request-breadth break-even where orchestration overhead stops paying for itself.
